text:
elena: Heads up — we just had a burst of GPU pod evictions in ap-southeast1-a, looks like fragmentation + a transient node NIC flap. Noticed a bunch of tiny pods piling on specific racks and then preemptions started. Anyone seen this pattern before?

sam: yep seen similar when warm-pool attach latency spikes and scheduler binpacking gets skewed. which fleets?

elena: mostly inference-gpu-prod and some canary batches from internal-ci. Node churn + a few taints applied by kubelet after conntrack errors.

rahul: digging events now, running `kubectl get events --all-namespaces --field-selector reason=Preempted` but quick grep showed `FailedAttachVolume` and `NetworkUnavailable` around the same timeframe.

ops-bot: alert: 3 pods evicted in inference-gpu-prod (ap-southeast1-a) in last 5m — reasons: Preempted, NodePressure, NetworkUnavailable.

kevin: can we get a heatmap of GPU slot occupancy by rack? suspect tiny-pod scattering + affinity rules forcing hot racks. if packing is greedy for memory then gpu-slot fragmentation happens.

lia: cost flag — if we start moving tiny-pod jobs to smaller instances we can defragment, but that means more egress and likely higher spot churn. what's the SLA tolerance?

sam: quick hypothesis: a label rollout last night added `gpu-type=rtx6000` selector on some deployments, so scheduler co-located a bunch on limited pool. when NIC flaps, node taints kicked in -> preempts cascade.

elena: confirmed: rollout PR #789 added `nodeAffinity` to internal-ci canaries. rolling it back now for canaries. production still has broad selectors tho.

rahul: posting relevant event chunk:
```
Warning  Preempted  2m  default-scheduler  Preempted by higher priority pod inference-worker-42
Warning  NodeNotReady  2m  kubelet  Node ap-se1-rack3-node7 not ready: network plugin down
Warning  Evicted  1m  kubelet  Pod evicted: node had condition: MemoryPressure
```

kevin: we should target three mitigations: 1) temporary soft-affinity to spread tiny pods, 2) reduce priority for non-prod tiny pods to avoid cascading preempts, 3) throttle canary rollouts in that AZ.

lia: agree. add cost note: spreading tiny pods increases tokenization throughput cost by ~8% but reduces eviction churn — cheaper than sustained retries.

elena: putting together an ops playbook now. immediate actions: rollback canary affinity, mark rack3 nodes unschedulable for new non-prod canaries, and launch a binpack defrag job to coalesce small pods onto warm nodes.

sam: for the defrag job, suggest using `kubectl drain --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --force` on specific tiny-node candidates with `PodDisruptionBudget` hooks so we don't hit prod.

rahul: I'll run queries to compute percent fragmentation per rack (gpu slots unused vs reserved). if we see >25% fragmentation on rack3 we'll run defrag.

ops-bot: note: scheduled maintenance window ap-southeast1-a in 2h — might be related.

kevin: long term: propose scheduler change to prefer balanced-gpu-packing metric (minimize per-rack variance) + telemetry for attach latencies to avoid affinity rollouts causing hotspots.

lia: let's also have finance model the cost of doing aggressive defrag vs buying larger uniform racks — send numbers to `#cost-ops`.

elena: thanks team. will update after rollback and initial defrag probe. tagging @oncall for visibility. :thumbsup:
